sentences.text:
This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed seeking the following relief:
"....to issue an appropriate Writ, Order Or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of respondent Nos.2 to 6 in failing to pass Award for the missing extent of an extent of 51 sq. yards out of 132 sq. yards in Sy. No. 1119 of Dubbhapally Village, H/o. Chelpur Village, Ghanapur Mandal,
Jayashankar Bhupalpally District, even though the preliminary notification under Act 30 of 2013 dated 21.05.2019 and final declaration dt 04.06.2020 declares that an extent of 132 sq. yards in Sy. No. 1119 mentioned was acquired but fail to pass award pursuant to the proceedings of the 2nd respondent No.G/204/2017 dt 22.08.2023 for the entire extent and limiting only to an extent of 81 sq yards and not passing Award for missing extent of 51 sq yards in the subsequent awards as per the provisions of Act 30 of 2013 till date along with benefits as illegal, arbitrary,
unconstitutional and consequently direct respondent Nos.2 to 6 to forthwith pass Award for the missing extent of 51 sq yards in Sy. No. 1119 of Dubbhapally Village,
H/o. Chelpur Village, Ghanapur Mandal, Jayashankar Bhupalpally District as per the preliminary and final notifications in the 4thPhase award out of 132 sq. yards along with all consequential benefits in the interest of justice..."

2. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
3.

It is the case of the petitioner that respondents Nos.2 and 3 acquired certain lands in Chelpur Village, including his land, for the purpose of construction of Budidha Kunta project (2nd Phase,
1x600 MW Thermal Power Project) to benefit the respondents Nos.5 and 6.
It is further case of the petitioner that a preliminary notification vide Rc.No.A/712/2015 was issued on 21.05.2019, wherein the petitioner's land in Sy.No.1119 was listed in Sl.No.182.
In the final declaration issued on 04.06.2020, the land was further divided and the petitioner's share of 132 sq. yards was mentioned in Sl.No.187.

It is further case of the petitioner that even though his land is listed in final declaration but in the 1st Phase Award passed on 04.06.2020, his total extent of land i.e, 132 sq. yards of land was not mentioned.

In the 2nd Phase Award vide Proceedings No.G/204/2017, dated 22.08.2023,
the respondent No.2 passed award only to an extent of 81 sq. yards, leaving 51 sq. yards.

It is stated that in the 4th Phase Award vide Proceedings No.G/204/2017, dated 07.12.2023, the 2nd respondent assured that missing extents from earlier phases, including the petitioner's remaining 51 sq. yards, would be considered.

Contrary to the said assurance, no award has been passed for the Potharapu Srikanth vs The State Of Telangana on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115067916/

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that since 2021, the respondents have extended the declaration several times, but failed to resolve the petitioner's claim, which action on the part of respondents amounts to violation of petitioner's rights under Articles 14, 21, and 300-A of Constitution of India and contrary to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ("RFCTLARR Act").
Therefore, the learned counsel prays this Court to direct the respondents to pass an award for the remaining 51 sq.yards in Sy.No.1119 situated at Dubbhapally Village H/o. Chelpur Village, Ghanapur Mandal, Jayashankar-Bhupalpally District.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, the learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition has not disputed the issuance of preliminary notification dated 21.05.2019 and final declaration dated 04.06.2020 by the respondents.

6. In view of the above submissions, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the respondents to examine the case of the petitioner for payment of compensation in respect of remaining extent of land i.e, 51 sq.yards in Sy.No.1119 situated at Dubbhapally Village H/o. Chelpur Village, Ghanapur Mandal, Jayashankar-Bhupalpally District and pass an award, strictly in accordance with the provisions of RFTCLARR Act, 2013 within a period of two(02) months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
7. With the above observations, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.

JUSTICE C.V.BHASKAR REDDY Date: 03.10.2024 scs Potharapu Srikanth vs The State Of Telangana on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115067916/
